adjudications.question: blocked decision consumes event_id and is never re-executed when data arrives late
adjudications.rationale: Verified in code and by a real test: test_late_data_emits_data_blocked_and_retry_resumes_same_event_id asserts the retry emits 0 and the ledger digest is unchanged. The decision is recorded (never skipped silently), no price is synthesized, no stale rank reused, and the deterministic event_id makes re-execution structurally impossible. For a forward observation this is the PIT-honest direction: re-executing on late data would create look-ahead. Completeness is representable because the blocked record exists and the dashboard surfaces blocked_decisions per family plus blocked chart markers — those must stay visible (condition C5). Loss of one slot is the conservative cost of honesty.

adjudications.question: order_intent_count derived as symbol-level target_weights entries across data_status=OK events
adjudications.call: ACCEPTABLE with labeling condition already satisfied
adjudications.rationale: The four counters remain distinct and a dedicated dashboard test proves non-conflation (two decisions / three intents / four fills / one closed). The derivation is disclosed in the UI legend ('symbol-level TARGET_INTENT entries emitted across decided events (an intent is NOT a fill)') — render.py:1103. Residual nuance: it counts symbol entries on no-change rebalances and counts zero on risk-blocked events whose intent existed; acceptable because the label does not claim 'orders that would be sent'. target_weights never contains zero-weight entries (verified in all three adapters), so there is no inflation path. Condition C6 keeps the label binding.

adjudications.question: A2 sell guard counts reducing-sell notional against gross; executor slices via headroom; safe+honest or remediation before activation?

adjudications.rationale: The guard is fail-closed: it can refuse valid trades, never permit leverage; fills that do occur are recorded exactly as they occur. But the headroom-aware slicing algorithm and the 0.5% notional buffer live only in tests/test_shv1_engine_smoke.py; if carried into production unchanged, the gross-1.0 sleeves would systematically execute ~0.5% under target and fragment fills into slices, biasing fill-level statistics — and if re-implemented ad hoc, the new code would be un-audited. The production executor work mandated by F1 must either fix the guard for reducing sells (subtract the reduction) or freeze the slicing+buffer as disclosed production bytes inside the scanned surface.
